title: The Beard Shaving

full_text:
Following the donkey ride into the cow manure, Guru Paramartha's magnificent silver beard had lost some of its pristine luster. Several hairs were singed by the exploding egg, and the Guru felt that a dignified trimming was urgently required.

The village barber, however, had raised his fee from two coppers to four coppers.

Guru Paramartha was indignant: 'Four copper coins for trimming twenty hairs? Outrageous extortion! Are we not self-sufficient philosophers? Matti, you shall be the ashram barber! Shave my neck and trim my beard with stately precision!'

Matti felt immensely honored: 'Master, my hand shall be as steady as Mount Meru!'

The disciples fetched an old, rusty sheep-shearing razor from the garden shed. Madayan mixed a bowl of cold well-water with laundry soap, producing a stiff, gray lather that smelled of sulfur.

The Guru sat upon the wooden stool, his chin elevated with dignified majesty. Matti lathered his master's face until the Guru looked like a snow-covered mountain.

Matti gripped the rusty razor with both hands, took a deep breath, and brought the blade down against the Guru's throat!

Because the razor was blunt and rusty, it did not slice the hairs; it caught them, pulled them, and scraped the tender skin like a rusty saw!

The Guru gasped, his eyes watering: 'Gently, Matti! You are skinning me like an onion!'

Matti apologized: 'Forgive me, Master! The lather is too thick; I cannot see where the beard ends and your chin begins!'

Peedan intervened: 'Allow me to illuminate the field of operation!'

Peedan lit a large oil torch and held it close to the Guru's face. But as Peedan leaned over to inspect the progress, his elbow bumped Matti's arm.

The sharp jolt caused Matti's hand to slip! The razor sliced off a large chunk of the Guru's left mustache, while the flame of Peedan's torch caught the soapy beard!

'PHUUUUFF!'

A flash of fire flared across the Guru's face! The dry beard burned with a terrifying crackle and a foul stench of singed hair!

The Guru leaped from his stool, screaming like a banshee: 'FIRE! MY BEARD IS BURNING!'

Mudan, reacting with swift presence of mind, grabbed the nearest bucket—which happened to be filled with dirty dye-water from the laundry basin—and hurled the entire contents squarely into Guru Paramartha's face!

The fire was extinguished, but the Guru stood dripping with purple dye, his magnificent silver beard burned to a charred, blackened stubble on the right, completely missing on the left, and his mustache vanished entirely!

The bronze mirror was brought. Looking upon his purple, charred, half-shaved countenance, Guru Paramartha stared in speechlessness for three full minutes.

Madayan nodded with profound artistic appreciation: 'A magnificent transformation, Master! You now possess the austere, terrifying countenance of an ancient Vedic warrior-sage!'

Wiping purple water from his eyebrows, Guru Paramartha croaked: 'Fetch me a shawl to cover my head, and pay the village barber five coppers to never speak of this day!'
moral: Entrusting a delicate blade to inexperienced hands invites bloodshed and comic disfigurement.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
